knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 3.3.3
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly describes a permutation hypothesis test?
knowledge_checks.body: Select the exchangeability → reference distribution move.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Permutation HT uses reshuffling under an exchangeable null. It is not a Normal cookbook z-test, not bootstrap CI construction, and not chi-square GOF.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Permute labels under exchangeability; compare the observed statistic to the permutation reference distribution.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Equating permutation with Normal z-tests, bootstrap CIs, or GOF.

choices.label: Under an exchangeability null, labels or assignments are permuted to build a reference distribution for the test statistic; the observed statistic is compared with that distribution.
A permutation test is identical to a Normal two-sample z-test; only the name changes.
Permutation tests estimate a confidence interval by resampling with replacement, the same way a bootstrap CI does.
Permutation tests are chi-square goodness-of-fit procedures that compare observed frequencies to a named distribution.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 3.3.3
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Under H₀ of no treatment effect, treatment labels are exchangeable across units. Which statement is correct?
knowledge_checks.body: Permutation move; refuse Normal-cookbook and GOF conflation.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: Permutation builds a null reference from exchangeability. Parametric Normal tests, GOF, and bootstrap CIs are different tools.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Exchangeability → permute → reference distribution; refuse Normal-cookbook and GOF conflation.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Treating permutation as optional flavour of a z-test, or swapping in GOF/bootstrap CI.

choices.label: Shuffle or reassign labels under H₀, recompute the test statistic many times, and compare the observed statistic to that permutation reference distribution. That is not a Normal two-sample z-test by another name, and not a chi-square GOF to a named distribution.
Compute a Normal two-sample z statistic once; permutation is only an optional label for that same parametric test.
Compare observed frequencies to Poisson expected counts with a chi-square GOF; that finishes the permutation requirement.
Resample with replacement to form a percentile confidence interval; reject H₀ if zero is outside that interval, and call the procedure a permutation test.

worked_example.title: Exact permutation test for two claim groups
worked_example.problem_statement: Small claim samples (£00): Group A = {10, 12, 14}, Group B = {8, 9, 11}. Test H₀: the two groups share the same distribution, using the two-sided permutation statistic |x̄_A − x̄_B|. Enumerate all C(6,3) = 20 assignments of three labels to A. The observed |x̄_A − x̄_B| equals 8/3. Exactly 4 of the 20 permutations have |diff| ≥ 8/3. Report the exact permutation p-value.
worked_example.attempt_before_reveal: CMP closed. Compute the observed |x̄_A − x̄_B|, then form p = (# extreme)/20.

steps.label: Observed difference
steps.explanation: The permutation test needs the observed value of the chosen statistic.

steps.label: Exact p-value
steps.attempt_cue: Divide the number of extreme permutations by 20.
steps.explanation: Under H₀ every assignment of three labels to A is equally likely; the p-value is the proportion at least as extreme as observed.

steps.label: Decision at α = 0.05
steps.explanation: Do not reject H₀ when p > α.

worked_example.final_answer: Observed |x̄_A − x̄_B| = 8/3; exact permutation p-value = 0.2; do not reject H₀ at α = 0.05.
worked_example.common_pitfall: Computing a two-sample t p-value on n = 3 per group and treating it as the permutation p-value, or reporting 4/C(6,3) incorrectly as 4/15 by mixing combinations with permutations of a different size.
